'''Municipality of Banguingui''' ([[Sinama language|Sinama]]: ''Lahat Banguingui''; [[Tausug language|Tausūg]]: ''Kawman sin Banguingui''; {{langx|tl|Bayan ng Banguingui}}) is a [[municipality of the Philippines|municipality]] in the [[Philippine Province|province]] of [[Sulu]], [[Philippines]]. According to the 2024 census, it has a population of 39,202 people.{{PH wikidata|population_reference}} From its original name '''Tongkil''', it was renamed ''Banguingui'' on January 29, 1999, by virtue of ''Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 71'' of the [[Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao]] in honor of the dominant [[Banguingui]] tribe of the municipality.{{cite web|title=Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 71; An Act Changing the Name of the Municipality of Tongkil in the Province of Sulu to the Municipality of Banguingui|url=http://rla-armmgov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/MMAA-71.pdf|website=Regional Legislative Assembly, Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao|accessdate=January 27, 2016}}{{Cite web |url=http://armm.gov.ph/armm-content/uploads/2013/03/MMA%20Act%20No.%2071.pdf |title=MMA Act No. 71 : An Act Changing the name of the Municipality of Tongkil in the Province of Sulu to the municipality of Banguingui |access-date=October 6, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903120347/http://armm.gov.ph/armm-content/uploads/2013/03/MMA%20Act%20No.%2071.pdf |archive-date=September 3, 2014 |url-status=dead }} It was inaugurated only on January 29, 2006.[http://www.vicegovladyann.com/Jan3109.html Banguingui municipality celebrates 10th anniversary]{{Dead link|date=November 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ==Geography== ===Barangays=== Tongkil is politically subdivided into 14 [[barangay]]s.
